chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'O you who have believed, testimony [for] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest [should be] two just men from you or others from outside.' (He quoted the verse up to 'min ghayrikum').
He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are two disbelievers.' I said: 'Two just men from you.' He said: 'Two Muslims.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the valid witnesses for a will according to Shia jurisprudence based on this verse?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Quranic verse 2:180 by interpreting 'two just men from you' as specifically referring to two Muslims, while 'others from outside' refers to non-Muslims (Kuffar). This establishes a hierarchical distinction in witness validity for wills, prioritizing Muslim witnesses while acknowledging the permissibility of non-Muslim witnesses in their absence, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence of inheritance and testimony.
